questions.question: During a trip, which of the following does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.correctAnswerText: Seat cushion
questions.explanation: During a trip, check your gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights regularly. Watch for any signs of trouble.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
Acceptable if you are eating foods that are easy to eat.

questions.correctAnswerText: A dangerous activity.
questions.explanation: Eating, smoking, or drinking while driving is distracting and dangerous. Plan ahead and stop to eat during long trips.

questions.question: Compared to talking on a cell phone while driving, texting while driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. It distracts your mind and takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle, the oil pressure should:

options.text: Gradually build up pressure over the span of a few minutes.
Come up to normal within a few seconds.
Start high, then decrease as the engine is run.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come up to normal within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal levels within a few seconds after the engine starts.

questions.question: How much water must be present for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A good amount, such as a large puddle

questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Try not to drive in fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try not to drive in fog.
questions.explanation: Avoid driving in fog if possible. If you must drive in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: Water on bridges:

options.text: Usually freezes before water on other parts of a roadway.
Usually freezes after water on other parts of a roadway.
Is not a concern in cool weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually freezes before water on other parts of a roadway.
questions.explanation: Water on bridges freezes before water on the rest of the road. Be extra careful on bridges when it is near freezing.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a cause for concern since it is stopped.
Is only a concern if passengers are exiting the bus.
Is a concern whether or not passengers are visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a concern whether or not passengers are visible.
questions.explanation: Always be careful around stopped buses. Passengers may be near the bus, and the bus may block your view or their view of you.

questions.question: One way to prevent fatigue on long trips is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks.
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Driving through the night or when you would normally be sleeping is especially dangerous.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Rely on the posted signals to indicate when a train is approaching.
Rely on the movements of other motorists to indicate when a train is approaching.
Not rely on signals to indicate when a train is approaching.
Look to see if nearby plants are moving from the breeze created by a passing train

questions.correctAnswerText: Not rely on signals to indicate when a train is approaching.
questions.explanation: Always assume a train is coming when you approach a railroad crossing. Do not depend only on signals or sounds to know if a train is near.

questions.question: Why should tires be checked regularly in very hot weather?

options.text: Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
The tread wears down extra quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Warm air expands. This means tire pressure can reach dangerous levels in hot weather. If this happens, stop and let your tires cool down. Do not let air out of the tires. If you do, the pressure will drop to an unsafe level when the tires cool.

questions.question: Why should tires be checked regularly in very hot weather?

options.text: Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
The tread wears down more quickly than in cooler weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases with temperature. Pay special attention to tire mounting and pressure when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, the vehicle should NOT be:

options.text: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
Parked within 40 feet of the road.
Parked for only short periods of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Do not park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Also do not park within 5 feet of the traveled part of a road. Park such vehicles only briefly.

questions.question: After changing a tire, the driver should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check if rocks have gotten into the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After driving a short distance with a new tire, stop and check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: When checking the windshield before a trip, you should do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Check your windshield for cracks or other problems that could block your view of the road. Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension. Check the wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and loose fasteners.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo is on fire, you should:

options.text: Try to put it out with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them fight the fire.
Hope the fire goes out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them fight the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire requires special training and protective equipment. Do not try to fight this type of fire yourself unless you are properly trained and equipped.

questions.question: If there are no warning gates or lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Not worry because the tracks are likely abandoned.
Park your vehicle and walk to the tracks to check for approaching trains.
Look down the tracks in both directions to check for approaching trains.
Do whatever the other vehicles around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look down the tracks in both directions to check for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no control devices like gates or warning lights. Before crossing, look down the tracks in both directions to make sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, you should begin by:

options.text: Turning the steering wheel in the direction you want to go.
Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want to go.
Turning the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, start by turning the steering wheel opposite to your desired direction. Once the trailer begins to turn, reverse your steering to follow the trailer's path.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to change gears. Release the accelerator, press the clutch in, and shift to neutral at the same time. Release the clutch and let the vehicle reach the correct speed. Then press the clutch in again, shift to the new gear, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to shift gears. It takes practice to become skilled at double clutching.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it down and release it repeatedly, but do not hold it down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down slowly.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal slowly and gradually.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out and call for help.
Keep trying to move the vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave it immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency numbers on signs near the crossing and call 911 or the number listed.

questions.question: What can a broken exhaust system do?

options.text: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: What should you do before looking under your vehicle's hood during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Set the parking brake and/or place chock blocks.
Leave the vehicle in a low gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set the parking brake and/or place chock blocks.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting under the hood, make sure the parking brake is set and the wheels are blocked with chock blocks.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, if you see fresh oil under your vehicle, what does this mean?

options.text: It is a problem that needs attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a problem that needs attention.
questions.explanation: During pre-trip inspection, check under the vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Any of these leaks is a problem.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives.

questions.question: Can you drive a truck if the trailer has ABS but the tractor does not?

options.text: No, the truck cannot be driven because both must have ABS.
Yes, but drive slower than normal.
No, you must find a different tractor with ABS.
Yes, the tractor and trailer can be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, the tractor and trailer can be used together.
questions.explanation: It is acceptable to use a tractor and trailer together even if only one has anti-lock brakes. The vehicle with ABS will have better braking control.

questions.question: What must emergency response information include?
questions.correctAnswerText: Fire and explosion risks
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include details about fire and explosion risks for the hazardous materials being transported.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Smoother steering
questions.explanation: Signs of tire failure include a loud bang, heavy vibration, and steering that becomes difficult. Steering does not become smoother during tire failure.

questions.question: How should an exhaust system be?
questions.correctAnswerText: Fastened tightly.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system must be securely fastened. All parts must be properly mounted and not touch moving parts of the vehicle.
